cards.text: It's the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede, made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans. Daniel, a man of Judah carried off to Babylon (Daniel 1:1-6), tells this part himself: he's reading the sacred books, and he comes to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet about Jerusalem's desolation. And friend, this man is doing the MATH.

cards.question: In the word of the LORD to Jeremiah, how long would the desolation of Jerusalem last?
So Daniel turns his attention to the Lord God, to seek Him by prayer and petition. What goes along with his prayer?

answers.text: A feast with music and dancing

cards.text: Then Daniel prays, and before he asks for ANYTHING, he starts with who God is: the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments. Friend, I open every phone call with "Hey, so, quick favor."

cards.question: When Daniel confesses, he talks about the people's sin but leaves himself out of it.
Daniel says they didn't listen to God's servants the ___, who spoke in His name to their kings, leaders, fathers and all the people.

cards.text: Daniel says righteousness belongs to God, but shame covers the people: the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in every country God drove them to because of their unfaithfulness. Their kings, leaders and fathers too, friend, so nobody's sneaking out the side door on this one.

cards.question: The people are covered with shame. But Daniel says something belongs to God, even though they rebelled against Him. What is it?

cards.text: No excuses, no "well, technically": Daniel says they didn't obey the voice of the LORD or walk in His laws, so the oath and the curse have been poured out on them.

cards.question: Daniel says the oath and the curse poured out on them were written in the Law of ___.

cards.text: Daniel says God has carried out the words spoken against them by bringing a great disaster. Under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what's been done to Jerusalem, and I think that one hurts to say.

cards.question: After all that disaster, Daniel says the people turned from their iniquities and sought the favor of the LORD.

cards.text: Daniel says the LORD kept the calamity in store and brought it upon them. For the LORD is righteous in all He does, yet they haven't obeyed His voice.

cards.question: Daniel reminds God how He brought His people out of the land of ___ with a mighty hand.

cards.text: After ALL that confessing, Daniel finally gets to his request. He prays that God's anger and wrath would turn away from His city Jerusalem, His holy mountain, and that God would cause His face to shine upon His desolate sanctuary.

cards.question: Daniel says they bring their petitions before God because of their own righteous acts.

cards.text: Then Daniel's prayer builds: "O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act!" Friend, that's a man asking with everything he's got.

cards.question: At the end of his prayer, Daniel asks God not to delay.

cards.text: Daniel is STILL praying, still confessing his own sin and the sin of his people Israel, still bringing his petition about God's holy mountain. Friend, my prayers usually wrap up when the oven timer dings.

cards.question: While Daniel is still praying, someone he had seen in an earlier vision comes to him in swift flight. Who is it?

cards.text: Gabriel, the one Daniel saw in the earlier vision (Daniel 8:16), arrives about the time of the evening sacrifice. He instructs Daniel and speaks with him.

cards.question: Gabriel instructs Daniel and speaks with him. What does Gabriel say he has come to give Daniel?
Gabriel says an answer to Daniel's prayer went out at the beginning of his petitions.

cards.text: Gabriel also tells Daniel he is highly precious, and friend, I came with a price sticker that said 25 cents. Then comes the message: seventy weeks are decreed for Daniel's people and his holy city.

cards.question: Seventy weeks are decreed for Daniel's people and holy city. What does Gabriel say they are decreed to do?

answers.text: Bring down the king of Persia
Send the people back to Egypt

cards.question: Gabriel says the seventy weeks are also decreed to bring in everlasting righteousness.

cards.text: The rest of what's decreed: to stop their transgression, to make atonement for iniquity, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place. Read that one slow, friend.
Gabriel gives a starting point: the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem. From there until the Messiah, the Prince, he counts seven weeks and sixty-two weeks.

cards.question: Gabriel says Jerusalem will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of ___.

cards.text: Gabriel goes on: "Then after the sixty-two weeks the Messiah will be cut off and will have nothing." Next, he says, the people of the prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary, and the end will come like a flood.

cards.question: Gabriel says there will be peace until the end.

cards.text: Gabriel says desolations have been decreed. Then he speaks of one who will confirm a covenant with many for one week.

cards.question: Gabriel speaks of one who will confirm a covenant with many for one week. In the middle of that week, what will this one put an end to?

cards.text: Then Gabriel says that on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, "…until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him." That's where his message ends, friend, and it's a heavy one.
